text:
anya: Heads up — I'm planning a small refactor to the ingress ownership window: move from a single lease token to a split token (route-lease + stream-lease) so we can do model-variant fallback without tearing the client connection. Goal: minimize midflight aborts and keep billing/metrics sane. Thoughts?

sam: curious — can you sketch sequence?

anya: quick sketch: client binds to route-lease (long-lived, tied to route and tenant). For each streaming request we mint a short-lived stream-lease for ownership of KV cache + model slot. If stream-lease is revoked we try to handoff to compatible model variant by issuing a new stream-lease with state transfer. If no variant available, we surface a graceful end-of-stream instead of abort.

ben (runtime): hmm. state transfer for KV cache is the tricky part. We have ~O(1) checkpoint bytes but the runtime expects contiguous KV pointers. Two options: copy-on-write snapshot + apply delta, or keep small resumable token that encodes last token index and client-side can request a soft resume from new slot. Both have tradeoffs on latency.

jess (sre): what about SLO surface? If handoff takes >100ms we may break p99 for streaming. We should cap attempts (like 2 handoffs) and instrument handoff latency and failure reasons. Also need to account for billing: a handoff shouldn't double-charge tokens.

anya: agreed on cap. Proposal: attempt one live handoff (<=150ms target) then fallback to final chunk + 503 soft-fail with reason header. Billing: on handoff success, mark tokens generated after new stream-lease as billed to new slot; tokens emitted during transition counted to original request but reconciled in billing job. We'll add a `handoff_id` to metering events.

sam: small ask — can we keep client-visible semantics simple? i.e., clients see either continuous stream or final error. No midstream duplicate tokens or reordered chunks.

anya: yes. We'll ensure handoff is atomic from client's POV: stream resumes with a short handshake frame `HANDOFF <handoff_id> <new_variant>` then payload continues. If we can't resume we emit `TERMINATE <reason>` and close.

ben (runtime): proto sketch for stream-lease token: ```json
{
  "lease_id":"uuid",
  "route":"r-abc",
  "variant":"redwood-quant-8bit-2026-03",
  "valid_until":1640000000,
  "kv_checkpoint":"b64...",
  "handoff_allowed":true
}
```
This keeps it compact. `kv_checkpoint` is base64 of small state. If absent, we fall back to stateless resume (client asks for soft continuation from last token index).

jess (sre): make sure `valid_until` is short (<=30s) to avoid stale ownership. Also add signature so proxies can verify without contacting control plane for every request. We already sign route-lease; reuse that keypair.

sam: signing is fine but proxies need to know which keys are trusted. That implies key rotation strategy. Any thoughts?

anya: reuse existing key rotation; embed `key_id` in token and let proxy fetch rotated public keys from control plane cache periodically. Keep cache TTL low (60s).

ben (runtime): concerning memory: storing checkpoints for many concurrent streams could blow us up. We should only materialize checkpoint if handoff is possible (based on route policy). Default: disabled for high-concurrency public routes. Enable for enterprise routes or dedicated capacity.

anya: yes — make `handoff_allowed` derived from route config and plan. Also expose a per-route knob: `handoff_budget` to limit concurrent handoffs. If budget exhausted, we decline handoff early and close gracefully.

jess (sre): observability: add metrics `handoff.attempts`, `handoff.success`, `handoff.latency_ms`, `handoff.fail_reason`. Also trace events: `handoff.requested` -> `handoff.granted` -> `handoff.completed`.

sam: rollout plan? This touches frontdoor, proxy, runtime, and billing pipelines. Prefer feature-flagged rollout by route tag.

anya: plan: implement tokens + proxy verification (no state transfer) behind flag first. Then runtime handles `kv_checkpoint` write+read and we enable handoff on 10% of enterprise routes. Then iterate.

ben (runtime): can we do a canary that simulates handoff but doesn't actually change model slots? i.e., test the token flow and handshake only, to validate latency and error cases.

anya: yes — a "dry-run" handoff mode that runs the handshake and logs metrics but always continues on same slot. Good idea.

jess (sre): don't forget chaos testing for transient network partitions during handoff. Add a small litmus test.

sam: minor nit — we need to update gateway docs and SDK error codes. Add a `HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE` code and `HANDOFF_IN_PROGRESS` event.

anya: noted. Action items: 1) I will open RFC with token format + handshake frames (PR by EOD). 2) Ben will prototype checkpoint shape and dry-run path. 3) Jess will sketch SLO dashboards and chaos tests. 4) Sam will draft SDK error codes and migration notes.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled for staging at 2026-03-25T03:00:00Z (canary flag off).

sam: thanks — looks good. Quick question: if handoff fails after we already emitted `HANDOFF` frame but before new payload starts, do we send `TERMINATE` or an idempotent no-op?

ben (runtime): send `TERMINATE` with `handshake_failed` reason. Clients should treat `TERMINATE` as final. We'll document retry semantics client-side (repost request).

anya: closing note — keep the API simple: from app dev POV, either continuous stream or final terminal event. All complexity stays server-side. We'll iterate on metrics to tune budgets.

sam: +1

ben (runtime): +1

jess (sre): +1 :thumbsup:
